intro.say: Earth is our home. Let us learn easy ways to keep it clean and happy!

rounds.say: Litter is rubbish dropped on the ground. It makes parks dirty and can hurt animals.
rounds.caption: litter

rounds.say: Always put rubbish in a bin. Some things can go in the recycling bin to be made into new things!
rounds.caption: bin it!

rounds.ask: You finish a juice box at the park. What should you do?

options.label: throw it on the grass
options.why: Litter on the grass can hurt animals.

options.label: hide it in a bush
options.why: Hidden litter is still litter.

rounds.explain: Putting rubbish in a bin keeps the park clean and animals safe.

rounds.ask: Which picture shows someone caring for Earth?

options.label: dropping litter
options.why: Dropping litter makes Earth dirty.

options.label: tap left running
options.why: A running tap wastes water.

rounds.explain: Planting trees gives animals homes and cleans the air.

rounds.ask: You are leaving the room. What should you do with the light?

options.label: leave it on
options.why: Lights left on waste electricity.

rounds.explain: Turning off lights saves electricity and helps the planet.

options.label: stop
options.why: That sign tells cars to stop.

options.label: heart
options.why: A heart means love, not recycling.

rounds.explain: The green arrows going round mean recycle: old things made into new things.

intro.say: Three magic words help our planet: reduce, reuse and recycle. Let us learn them!

rounds.say: Reduce means use less. Recycle means old things get made into new things. Paper, plastic, glass and cans can all be recycled.
rounds.caption: reduce · recycle

rounds.say: Reuse means use something again. Take a cloth bag to the shop again and again instead of a new plastic bag.
rounds.caption: reuse

rounds.explain: Sorting things the right way means they can be made into new things.

rounds.ask: Taking the same cloth bag to the shop every week is…

options.label: recycling
options.why: Recycling makes it into something new; here we use it again.

options.label: wasting
options.why: Using it again saves things from the bin.

rounds.explain: Using the same bag again and again is reusing.

rounds.ask: How can you save water when brushing your teeth?

options.label: let the tap run
options.why: A running tap wastes lots of water.

options.label: brush faster in the shower
options.why: A long shower uses lots of water.

rounds.explain: Turning off the tap while you brush saves lots of clean water.

rounds.ask: An empty glass jar can be reused. Which is a good new job for it?

options.label: throw on the road
options.why: Broken glass on the road is dangerous.

options.label: bury it in the park
options.why: Glass in the park could hurt someone.

rounds.explain: A clean jar makes a great pencil pot, so it gets a second job.

rounds.ask: Which is a way to reduce, or use less?

options.label: lights on all day
options.why: That uses more electricity, not less.

options.label: drive to the next house
options.why: A car uses fuel even for tiny trips.

rounds.explain: Walking or cycling uses no fuel and keeps the air cleaner.

intro.say: Let us think like Earth helpers. Why do our choices matter, and what is the best choice?

rounds.say: Plastic that ends up in the sea can hurt turtles, fish and birds. It can stay there for hundreds of years.
rounds.caption: plastic hurts sea animals

rounds.say: Food scraps like peels can go in a compost bin. They rot into rich soil that helps plants grow.
rounds.caption: compost

rounds.ask: Why is plastic in the ocean a big problem?

options.label: It makes the sea warm
options.why: Plastic does not heat the sea.

options.label: Animals can get hurt by it
It turns into fish
options.why: Plastic never turns into living things.

rounds.explain: Sea animals can get tangled in plastic or eat it by mistake.

rounds.ask: Where should a banana peel go?

options.label: recycling bin
options.why: Recycling is for paper, plastic, glass and cans, not food.

options.label: on the floor
options.why: Peels on the floor are slippery and messy.

rounds.explain: A peel rots in the compost and turns into soil for plants.

rounds.ask: Which is the BEST choice for a drink at school?

options.label: a new plastic cup every day
options.why: Lots of cups make lots of rubbish.

options.label: a new can every day
options.why: Even recycled cans use energy to make again.

rounds.explain: A refillable bottle is reused every day, so there is much less rubbish.
Cans and paper get recycled, food scraps get composted, and bags and clothes get used again.

rounds.ask: Why should we turn off lights and screens we are not using?

options.label: to make them dusty
options.why: Dust is not the reason.

options.label: so they get hot
options.why: Turning them off stops them using power.

rounds.explain: Making electricity often burns fuel, so using less helps keep the air clean.

rounds.ask: Old toys you no longer play with. What is the most caring thing to do?

options.label: throw them in the bin
options.why: They would be wasted in the bin.

options.label: leave them outside
options.why: Rain would spoil them.

rounds.explain: Giving toys away reuses them, so they are loved again and not wasted.
